name: limit_direction_from_a_curved_edge
why: A CURVED EDGE IS NOT A DIRECTION: the edge of a hole is a circle, and it gives the tangent at a point that nobody chose -- a part that looks right. The operation refuses it, saying that a straight edge or an axis made with «create_axis» is needed.
_why_it_was_a_fake_test: THE C# CHECK OF THIS GUARD WAS GREEN AND MEASURED NOTHING, and this was found out while writing this file. It said: «a curved edge does not appear among the edges the state lists, so the model cannot name it, so the guard is not reachable» -- and it verified it by counting the edges with «straight»: false. THAT FIELD DOES NOT EXIST. The state writes «curved»: true on non-straight edges and writes «straight» on none, so TryGetValue always failed, the count stayed at zero and the green was guaranteed whatever the part. Measured here: after a through hole the state offers TWO curved edges, the model can name them perfectly well, and the road that was believed closed has always been open.

expect._why_zero: a plate has twelve edges and they are all straight: it is the benchmark for the next step

expect.tolerance_why: the diameter is read from CylinderParams

expect._why_two: the two round edges of the through hole, one per face. It is THIS number that makes the case possible: they are edges that the state lists and that the model can name
